correctness.rationale: For \(0<\lambda\le1/2\), the assumed support functionals give both weighted chord norms at least \(\lambda J(X)+1-2\lambda\), exactly matching the published upper estimate. The identity \(J(\lambda,X)=J(1-\lambda,X)\) extends equality to all weights. For the affine-regular hexagon, a complete four-edge reduction proves \(J(H)=3/2\); the pair \(x=(1,1/2)\), \(y=(0,1)\) and functionals \(f_+(s,t)=t\), \(f_-(s,t)=s-t\) satisfy every hypothesis exactly.
risks: The theorem depends on the published weighted-James upper estimate; the proof explicitly restricts to the half interval where that estimate is used and extends by an independently proved symmetry identity.
The checker samples rational weights only; all universal quantifiers are established symbolically in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 article was inspected through the weighted-James definition, Theorem 5.2 and its surrounding corollaries. It gives inequalities but no supporting-face equality criterion and no affine-regular-hexagon profile. Public literature searches covered exact notation, equality/saturation terminology, support-functional aliases, the candidate formula, and the hexagonal object. The closest same-invariant published-result record concerns real sequence spaces; the closest same-object records concern different invariants. Overlap checks against the available prior-result corpus found a regular-octagon weighted profile but no statement implying the accepted theorem.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent equality condition may be stated in unindexed literature using exposed-face or support-face terminology rather than weighted-James terminology.
The affine-regular hexagon is linearly equivalent to several alternative coordinate normalizations, so an equivalent isolated computation could be catalogued under another model.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The result converts a published universal inequality into a reusable equality mechanism: one James-extremal pair and two compatible supporting faces determine the entire one-parameter weighted profile. This is structurally stronger than a single constant evaluation. The affine-regular hexagon is a canonical uniformly non-square Banach plane, and its complete profile demonstrates that the source upper envelope can remain sharp for every weight even when \(J(X)<2\). The criterion can therefore guide exact computations on other polyhedral spaces by reducing a parameter family to support-face incidence.
risks: The equality criterion is sufficient rather than a full classification of all saturation mechanisms.
